title: Kerala House: VR walkthrough
oneLiner: Walk through a two-storey Kerala house, its garden and play yard, in VR on a Meta Quest 3 or in any desktop browser.
heroAlt: The Kerala house model: a two-storey house with a tiled roof, timber veranda and balcony, set in a walled garden with a play yard

gallery.alt: Close view of the house in flat colour: carved fascia, shuttered windows, brass-banded pillars and a balcony ring
Grey overview of the whole compound: house, walled garden, play yard and palms outside the wall
Early grey blockout of the house, staircase, paths, trees and fence

blurb: A two-storey Kerala house with a timber veranda, a balcony ring, an outside staircase, a walled garden and a play yard. Walk the gate, the hall and the kitchen, climb to the balcony, or teleport around the grounds.
ctaNote: OPENS IN A NEW TAB · BEST ON META QUEST 3, ALSO WORKS ON DESKTOP
galleryHeading: From grey blockout to walkable house
galleryLede: The house was modelled in Blender, then exported as one small file with flat colours and no textures, so it loads fast even on a headset.
how: Model.
Built in Blender with a script, so the whole house can be rebuilt in one run. About 61,000 triangles, 39 flat-colour materials, 1.2 MB.
Engine.
A-Frame (WebXR), loaded from a fixed version. No app to install: it is a web page.
Walkable by name.
Anything named for walking (floors, steps, stairs, paths) can be stood on or teleported to. Everything else blocks you, so walls, furniture and railings behave.
Smooth stairs.
The floor under you is followed with easing, so climbing the outside stairs to the balcony feels steady.
Reset.
One button clears the model from memory and reloads it, which keeps a long headset session stable.
controls: Space to walk, arrows or WASD to steer, R to reset
status: Checked on desktop: the route from the gate to the hall, kitchen and back door, the stairs up to the balcony, wall and furniture blocking, and reset. Next pass: tuning controller aim, comfort and frame rate on the headset.

title: Human Respiratory System: XR anatomy atlas
oneLiner: Fly through a hologram of the human airway, lungs, heart and diaphragm in VR on a Meta Quest 3 or in any desktop browser.
heroAlt: A cyan hologram of the human body in wire mesh with the airway, both lungs, heart and diaphragm inside, labelled, beside a floating XR control panel
blurb: A life-size hologram of the human respiratory system. Follow a breath from the nose down the trachea into 18 branching paths, scale the body up to 40 times, explode the organs apart, isolate one system at a time and watch cyan air go in and warm air come out on a breath cycle you control.
ctaNote: OPENS IN A NEW TAB · BEST ON META QUEST 3, ALSO WORKS ON DESKTOP

gallery.alt: Exploded X-ray view: the ribcage, heart, vessels and trachea separated from the torso shell, with the labels and the control panel
Lungs isolated: two violet lungs with cyan breath particles moving along the airway, everything else faded to a faint outline
Bronchial tree isolated in X-ray view, showing the branching airways inside the faded body

galleryHeading: Four ways to look at one breath
galleryLede: The same model in different views: exploded, with one system isolated, and through the X-ray preset.
how: Model.
Modelled in Blender: body, ribcage, nose to bronchi, both lungs (3 lobes right, 2 left), heart with great vessels and the diaphragm. About 107,000 triangles, 2.2 MB.
Lighting.

The lighting is baked into the model itself: a cyan key light, a violet rim light and ambient occlusion, written into the vertex colours. The headset draws it unlit, so it looks the same everywhere and runs fast.
Airflow.

The 18 breathing paths (10 into the right lung, 8 into the left) were exported from the bronchial tree. The particles ride them: cyan air in, warm amber air out, on a 12 breaths per minute cycle you can change.
Locomotion.

A museum display, not a world to walk around: you ride a smooth circle round the organ you pick, always facing it. Pick an organ in the menu and you glide to it while everything else goes translucent. Hold either stick to the side to circle it, click a stick to exit, run its function, and finish its two tasks.
Reset.
One button throws the model out of memory and loads it again, which keeps a long headset session stable.
Explode.

Explode fades the body shell right out and draws a circulation diagram between the pieces: blue tubes for low-oxygen blood returning from the body and going to the lungs, red tubes for oxygen-rich blood coming back and leaving through the aorta, with moving dots showing the flow.
controls: Point at a panel button or a label and pull the trigger. Both hands show a laser
Circle the focused organ in a perfect circle. Pull a trigger while holding it to speed up
Exit the focused organ and return to the whole body (also the EXIT FOCUS button)
A cycles the view (deep X-ray is the default), B changes the circling speed
X resets the view, Y resets the experience
A and D to circle, W and S closer and further, Q and E lower and raise, 1 to 7 to focus an organ, O to circle hands-free, U for its function, R to reset
status: Checked on desktop: loading, the circling path (constant radius and height, always facing the organ), focus and translucency, the laser click path, explode, isolate, the three view presets, the breath cycle, reset and reload. Not yet felt on the headset: laser visibility, trigger response, circling speed.

title: Museum Floor: three masterpieces in three corners
oneLiner: Walk a gallery floor built in the language of the Bihar Museum, on a Meta Quest 3 or in any desktop browser.
heroAlt: Looking down the tapering sandstone corridor, lit by recessed vertical slots, into the dim hall with the bust of Nefertiti standing in a pool of light at the end

gallery.alt: Stephenson's Rocket on its low platform in the south-east corner, picked out by a concealed light slot in the alcove soffit
The triangular hall: a red travertine wall on the left, a backlit teak screen on the right, a near-black floor, and the bust of Nefertiti lit in the open ahead of her alcove
The bust of Nefertiti close up on her plinth out in the hall, lit from three sides against the glowing teak screen
The bust of Julius Caesar on a plinth in the south-west alcove, his label stand beside him

blurb: A gallery floor after the Bihar Museum in Patna: a lobby with backlit teak screens, a corridor that tapers open with light slots cut into leaning sandstone, and a triangular hall whose three corners are cut back into alcoves. A bust of Julius Caesar and Stephenson's Rocket stand one to a corner, and the bust of Nefertiti stands free in front of hers, under an elliptical skylight, where you can walk a full circle round her. Each of the three labels stands in the same place in its own corner.
ctaNote: OPENS IN A NEW TAB · BEST ON META QUEST 3, ALSO WORKS ON DESKTOP
galleryLede: The building compresses you in a corridor before it opens into the hall, which is how the real museum introduces its galleries. Every surface was lit once in Blender and baked into a texture, so the headset renders the whole floor without computing a single light.
how: Model.
Built in Blender with a script, so the whole floor can be rebuilt in one run. About 16,000 triangles in 11 groups, 2.4 MB.
Light.

Lit in Cycles behind a light-tight shell, so the only light is the designed light: a raking sun through slot windows, two skylight dishes, warm emission behind the teak, and a tight spot on each piece. The room is deliberately kept dim and the spots are not, so each masterpiece stands in its own pool of light.
Baked, not computed.
Each group is unwrapped and baked to its own atlas, then re-imported as pure emission. The room needs no lights at runtime; the only lights in the page are the three over the sculptures.
Walkable by name.

The floors are one mesh named for walking; everything else blocks. The masterpieces sit outside the collision world, with three invisible boxes standing in for them, so no raycast ever touches their 384,000 triangles.
One rule for three corners.

Each alcove shares the same local frame, so the label stand that reads best, the Rocket's, is measured once in that frame and the other two are that same stand rotated 120 and 240 degrees round the hall. Caesar and the Rocket end up with identical clearance, 1.12 m, which is how you know they match.
Compressed, not simplified.
Caesar and the Rocket ship at the full resolution of their scans, 160,000 and 169,000 triangles, Draco-compressed to 1.3 and 1.4 MB. The decoder is served from the site rather than a CDN.
Walk and fly.

The same locomotion as the Kerala house. Fly up through the skylight opening and you end up inside the dome. Flight is bound three ways, because A is a Quest button and a strafe key at the same time: the A button, the right grip, and a Fly button that stays on screen in the flat view.
controls: Walk where you aim, and hold it with the stick to go faster
Walk back to the information board
Space to walk, arrows or WASD to steer, F to fly, E and Q for height, P for the board, R to reset
status: Checked on desktop by driving the page's own components, not the camera: the walk from the lobby through the corridor into the hall (it stops at the bench at z 5.3), a full circle round Nefertiti still clear at 2.2 m, all four stands raycast-tested as standing inside nothing, and flight driven at a fixed timestep, climbing 1.6 to 5.2 m in three seconds and gliding at the full 4.5 m/s. Not yet felt on the headset: controller aim, frame rate, and whether the board and the three labels read at the right distance.

title: Kolkata Street: a monsoon tram scene
oneLiner: Stand in a wet Kolkata street under monsoon cloud, with trams, Ambassador taxis and a mosque at the end of the road, in VR on a Meta Quest 3 or in any browser.
heroAlt: Looking down a wet Kolkata street from above a tram: shuttered shopfronts and balconies on both sides, yellow Ambassador taxis, trolley wires, and a white mosque with a dome at the far end

gallery.alt: From a second-floor balcony, looking down through the scaffold at a red tram and yellow taxis on the wet road
A hand-span above the road: the wet street, the tram tracks and the tram ahead are reflected in the puddles
A red Calcutta tram number 5 facing you, an Ambassador taxi close in the foreground and the mosque dome behind
The street running live in the browser, with the viewpoint list on the right and the controls panel at the bottom left

blurb: A stretch of Kolkata about 250 metres long, built as a world rather than a model: two lines of shuttered shopfronts and balconies, tram tracks down the middle, trolley wire overhead, a scatter of small figures, and a white domed mosque closing the far end. Walk it at street level, fly up to the balcony and the wires, or jump between ten camera viewpoints, each named for a lens.
ctaNote: OPENS IN A NEW TAB · BEST ON META QUEST 3, ALSO WORKS ON DESKTOP AND PHONE
galleryHeading: One street, ten ways to stand in it
galleryLede: The street was modelled and lit in Blender, then rebuilt for the browser from the same layout. The first three pictures are renders; the last is the street running live.
how: Kit of parts.

The street is 25 assets: six building types, a mosque, sheds and hoardings, two trees, tram poles, a handcart, an auto-rickshaw, eight figures, the Ambassador taxi and the tram. Each is modelled once in Blender and exported to the web.
Placed from a layout.
A single layout file lists 118 placements. The page loads each model once and clones it wherever it is used, so 45 buildings cost one building's worth of memory.
Streams in.
The ground arrives first, so within a second there is a road to stand on and the rest builds up around you. About 8.5 MB of models, under 2 MB over the wire once compressed.
Walkable by name.
The road and footpaths are meshes named for walking. A ray follows them under your feet, so the kerb and the camber of the road feel steady.
Wet road.
The carriageway is near-black with very low roughness and a strong sky reflection, which is what makes a monsoon street look wet from a low angle.
Viewpoints.
Ten saved cameras, from a tram nose at 85 mm to a wide 24 mm in the road, reproduce the shots of the Blender render. In VR only your heading is set, never your pitch, so it stays comfortable.
Trams.
Press T and the two trams run the length of the street and loop. In VR the shadows are switched off to hold frame rate.
controls: W A S D walk, drag to look, Shift run, F walk or fly, E and Q up and down, 1 to 0 for the viewpoints, V next view, R reset, T run the trams
Drag to look, and the View buttons step between the ten viewpoints
status: Checked on desktop: loading from the page, the ten viewpoints, walking and flying, the trams, and reset. Not yet felt on the headset: comfort, frame rate and controller response.
